records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a new speech
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech of God to Moses, as in 1:1. The speech runs to the end of the chapter. It sets penalties for many of the acts already forbidden in chapter 18 and in 19:31.

records.heading: Penalties for sin

records.source: וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לתֹּאמַר֒ אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֩ מִבְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּמִן־הַגֵּ֣ר׀הַגָּ֣ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן מִזַּרְע֛וֹ לַמֹּ֖לֶךְ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת עַ֥ם הָאָ֖רֶץ יִרְגְּמֻ֥הוּ בָאָֽבֶן׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of Israel you will say, [a] man, [a] man of [the] sons of Israel and of the sojourners who sojourn in Israel who gives of his offspring to Molech, surely he will be put to death; [the] people of the land will stone him with stone[s].
pieces: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: '{{gender:Anyone|Any man}} from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, or from the outsiders living in Israel, who gives any of {{gender:their|his}} children to Molech, to be made to pass through the fire, must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone {{gender:that person|him}}.

L.2: "And to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel you will say, '{{gender:Anyone|Any man}} of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel or of the sojourners who sojourn in Israel who gives any of his offspring to Molech will surely be put to death; the people of the land will stone him with stones.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this: '{{gender:Someone|A man}} from Israel, or a stranger living in Israel, might give one of {{gender:their|his}} children to be burned as a sacrifice to the god Molech. That person must be put to death. The people of the community must throw stones at {{gender:that person|him}} until {{gender:that person dies|he dies}}.

decisions.choice: gives any of his offspring to Molech: hands over a child to the god Molech, to be burned as an offering
decisions.reason: The word for offspring is the word for seed, meaning a person's children. On Molech see 18:21, where the same act is forbidden. Elsewhere the act is described as making a son or daughter pass through the fire (Deuteronomy 18:10; 2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 32:35).

decisions.choice: a man, a man ... or of the sojourners: anyone at all, Israelite or outsider
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "anyone", as in 17:3. The law binds the outsiders who live in Israel as well as Israelites (17:8; on the sojourner see 16:29 and 19:10). Molech worship is not allowed to anyone who lives in the LORD's land.

decisions.choice: surely put to death ... the people of the land will stone him: the community carries out the death penalty by stoning
decisions.reason: "Surely put to death" doubles the verb for emphasis and is the standard wording of a death sentence (Exodus 21:12-17). "The people of the land" here means the whole community of Israel, who act together, as in 24:14-16 and Numbers 15:35-36. Stoning is the form of execution named for this and for the medium in verse 27.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "seed". Literal says "offspring"; Balanced and Readable say "children".

decisions.choice: to be made to pass through the fire (Balanced); to be burned as a sacrifice (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "gives ... to Molech". Balanced and Readable say what the giving was, in the wording used at 18:21.

decisions.choice: must throw stones at that person until that person dies
decisions.reason: Readable explains what stoning is. Readable also says "the people of the community" for "the people of the land".

records.source: וַאֲנִ֞י אֶתֵּ֤ן אֶת־פָּנַי֙ בָּאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ מִקֶּ֣רֶב עַמּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י מִזַּרְעוֹ֙ נָתַ֣ן לַמֹּ֔לֶךְ לְמַ֗עַן טַמֵּא֙ אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וּלְחַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And I, I will set my face against the man that, and I will cut off him from [the] midst of his people, for of his offspring he has given to Molech so as to make unclean my sanctuary and to profane [the] name of my holiness.
pieces: I myself will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against {{gender:that person|that man}} and will cut {{gender:them|him}} off from among the people. For by giving a child to Molech, {{gender:that person has|he has}} made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary unclean and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name.

L.3: And I, I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against {{gender:that person|that man}}, and I will cut him off from among his people, for he has given of his offspring to Molech, so as to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary unclean and to profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name.

R.3: I myself will turn against that person. I will remove {{gender:them|him}} from the people. By giving a child to Molech, that person has made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place unclean. That person has dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name.

decisions.choice: I will set my face against him and cut him off: God himself acts against the offender
decisions.reason: On setting the face against someone see 17:10. The emphatic "I" stresses that God acts as well as the community. Verse 4 shows why: if the people fail to carry out the sentence, God will still punish. On being cut off see 7:20.

decisions.choice: to make my sanctuary unclean and to profane my holy name: the sin damages God's dwelling and his reputation
decisions.reason: Worship of Molech is not a private act. It makes the LORD's sanctuary unclean, even when done far from it, because the people's sin pollutes the place where he lives among them (15:31; 16:16). To profane is to treat what is holy as common (10:10); the LORD's name is profaned when his people act as if he were one god among others (18:21; 19:12; 22:32).

decisions.choice: dishonored my holy name (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "profane". Readable says "dishonored" for a name, as at 19:12. Readable calls the sanctuary "my holy place".

records.source: וְאִ֡ם הַעְלֵ֣ם יַעְלִימֽוּ֩ עַ֨ם הָאָ֜רֶץ אֶת־עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ מִן־הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא בְּתִתּ֥וֹ מִזַּרְע֖וֹ לַמֹּ֑לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הָמִ֥ית אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if indeed they hide [the] people of the land their eyes from the man that when he gives of his offspring to Molech so as not to put to death him,
pieces: If the people of the land look the other way when {{gender:that person|that man}} gives one of {{gender:their|his}} children to Molech, and do not put {{gender:that person|him}} to death,

L.4: And if the people of the land indeed hide their eyes from {{gender:that person|that man}} when he gives of his offspring to Molech, so as not to put him to death,

R.4: The people of the community might pretend not to see when someone gives a child to Molech. They might not put that person to death.

decisions.choice: hide their eyes from him: deliberately ignore what he has done
decisions.reason: To hide the eyes is to look away on purpose and refuse to act (1 Samuel 12:3; Proverbs 28:27; Ezekiel 22:26). The doubled verb stresses it: the people knowingly let the crime go.

decisions.choice: so as not to put him to death: the community fails to carry out the sentence of verse 2
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 5, which gives God's response.

decisions.choice: The people of the community might ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the case in two sentences, and gives the result in verse 5.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י אֲנִ֧י אֶת־פָּנַ֛י בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא וּבְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י אֹת֜וֹ וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־הַזֹּנִ֣ים אַחֲרָ֗יו לִזְנ֛וֹת אַחֲרֵ֥י הַמֹּ֖לֶךְ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: and I will set I my face against the man that and against his clan, and I will cut off him and all [those who] act as prostitutes after him, by acting as prostitutes after the Molech, from [the] midst of their people.
pieces: then I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against {{gender:that person|that man}} and {{gender:their|his}} family, and I will cut off from among the people both {{gender:that person|him}} and all who follow {{gender:them|him}} in prostituting themselves to Molech.

L.5: then I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against {{gender:that person|that man}} and against his clan, and I will cut off him and all who prostitute themselves after him, prostituting themselves after Molech, from among their people.

R.5: Then I will turn against that person and against that person's family. I will remove that person from the people. I will also remove all who join in worshiping Molech. They are being unfaithful to me like a wife who chases other men.

decisions.choice: his clan: his wider family
decisions.reason: The word means a family group larger than a household. The family that shelters the offender shares his guilt. God's judgment reaches those who protect the guilty, not only the one who sinned.

decisions.choice: prostituting themselves after Molech: worshiping another god, unfaithful to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 17:7, worship of another god is called prostitution, because Israel belongs to the LORD as a wife to her husband (Exodus 34:15-16). Verse 6 uses the same picture for those who turn to mediums.

decisions.choice: They are being unfaithful to me like a wife who chases other men.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of prostitution in a separate sentence, as at 17:7. Literal and Balanced keep the image.

records.source: וְהַנֶּ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּפְנֶ֤ה אֶל־הָֽאֹבֹת֙ וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים לִזְנ֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־פָּנַי֙ בַּנֶּ֣פֶשׁ הַהִ֔וא וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the person who turns to the mediums and to the spiritists to act as a prostitute after them, and I will set my face against the person that and I will cut off him from [the] midst of his people.
pieces: If anyone turns to mediums and spiritists, and so prostitutes themselves by following them, I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against that person and cut them off from among the people.

L.6: And the person who turns to the mediums and to the spiritists, to prostitute himself after them, I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against that person, and I will cut him off from among his people.

R.6: Someone might go for help to people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits. That is being unfaithful to me. I will turn against that person. I will remove that person from the people.

decisions.choice: the mediums and the spiritists: people who claim to call up the dead and to learn secret things from spirits
decisions.reason: The first word can mean the spirit of a dead person (Isaiah 29:4) or the one who calls it up, as the woman at Endor did for Saul (1 Samuel 28:7-15). The second comes from the verb "know" and names one who claims special knowledge from such spirits. The two are always named together (19:31; Deuteronomy 18:11; 2 Kings 21:6). See 19:31, where turning to them is forbidden.

decisions.choice: the person: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word for person includes men and women alike (2:1; 4:2). Verse 27 names a man or a woman as the medium.

decisions.choice: to prostitute himself after them: to seek guidance from them instead of from the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. To go to the dead for guidance is unfaithfulness to the living God (Isaiah 8:19). Here God himself acts; the sentence of death for the medium follows in verse 27.

decisions.choice: people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "mediums and spiritists", as at 19:31. Readable describes what both do.

records.source: וְהִ֨תְקַדִּשְׁתֶּ֔ם וִהְיִיתֶ֖ם קְדֹשִׁ֑ים כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will consecrate yourselves and you will be holy, for I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Keep yourselves consecrated, and be holy, because I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.7: And you will consecrate yourselves, and you will be holy, for I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.7: Set yourselves apart as holy. Be holy, because I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: consecrate yourselves and be holy: keep yourselves set apart for the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself holy, here by keeping away from Molech and the mediums of verses 2-6. The call to be holy because the LORD is holy is explained at 11:44 and 19:2. Verse 8 adds that it is the LORD who makes them holy.

decisions.choice: for I am the LORD your God: the reason for the command
decisions.reason: On this formula see 18:2. Israel is to be holy because of who their God is.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־חֻקֹּתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will keep my statutes and you will do them; I [am] Yahweh [who] sets you apart as holy.
pieces: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and follow them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I make you holy.

L.8: And you will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes you holy.

R.8: Obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and do what they say. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am the one who makes you holy.

decisions.choice: keep my statutes and do them: obey God's laws in practice
decisions.reason: On "statutes" see 18:4. "Keep" and "do" together mean to obey carefully and to put into practice.

decisions.choice: the LORD who makes you holy: Israel's holiness is God's work as well as their duty
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of verse 7, now with God as subject. Israel is commanded to be holy, yet it is the LORD who sets them apart for himself (Exodus 31:13; Leviticus 21:8; 22:32). Verses 24 and 26 say how: he has separated them from the peoples.

records.source: כִּֽי־אִ֣ישׁ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְקַלֵּ֧ל אֶת־אָבִ֛יו וְאֶת־אִמּ֖וֹ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת אָבִ֧יו וְאִמּ֛וֹ קִלֵּ֖ל דָּמָ֥יו בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For [a] man, [a] man who curses his father and his mother, surely he will be put to death; his father and his mother he has cursed; his blood [is] on him.
pieces: {{gender:Anyone|Any man}} who curses father or mother must be put to death. Since {{gender:they have|he has}} cursed father or mother, the guilt for {{gender:their|his}} death is {{gender:their|his}} own.

L.9: For {{gender:anyone|any man}} who curses his father or his mother will surely be put to death; he has cursed his father and his mother; his blood [is] on him.

R.9: {{gender:Anyone|Any man}} who curses a father or mother must be put to death. That person has cursed a parent and is to blame for {{gender:their|his}} own death.

decisions.choice: curses his father or his mother: speaks of them with contempt, wishing them harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to make light of someone, to treat with contempt, and so to curse. It is the opposite of honoring father and mother (Exodus 20:12; Leviticus 19:3). The same penalty is given in Exodus 21:17. "Father and mother" means either one.

decisions.choice: his blood is on him: he alone bears the guilt for his death
decisions.reason: "Blood" here means guilt for a death, as in 17:4. When the community puts the offender to death, his blood does not stain those who carry out the sentence; the guilt rests on him, because his own act brought it about (Joshua 2:19; 2 Samuel 1:16; Ezekiel 18:13). The phrase is repeated in verses 11, 12, 13, 16 and 27, for each sentence of death by the community.

decisions.choice: for: verse 9 begins the list of penalties
decisions.reason: The small word that begins the verse can mean "for" or simply introduce a new case. It ties the laws that follow to the call of verse 8 to keep God's statutes.

decisions.choice: the guilt for their death is their own (Balanced); is to blame for their own death (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "his blood is on him". Balanced and Readable say what it means. The same wording is used in verses 11-16 and 27.

decisions.choice: their (Balanced and Readable, inclusive)
decisions.reason: The law applies to sons and daughters alike. Literal keeps "he" and "his"; Balanced and Readable avoid a male pronoun.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִנְאַף֙ אֶת־אֵ֣שֶׁת אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִנְאַ֖ף אֶת־אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ מֽוֹת־יוּמַ֥ת הַנֹּאֵ֖ף וְהַנֹּאָֽפֶת׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who commits adultery with [the] wife of [a] man, who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor, surely he will be put to death, the adulterer and the adulteress.
pieces: When a man commits adultery with a married woman, the wife of a fellow Israelite, the man and the woman who have committed adultery must both be put to death.

L.10: And a man who commits adultery with the wife of a man, who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor, will surely be put to death, the adulterer and the adulteress.

R.10: A man might have sexual relations with another man's wife, the wife of someone in Israel. Then both the man and the woman must be put to death.

decisions.choice: commits adultery: has sexual relations with another man's wife
decisions.reason: Adultery is forbidden in the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:14) and in 18:20. Here the penalty is set: death for both the man and the married woman (Deuteronomy 22:22). The law names the woman as guilty with the man, not as a victim.

decisions.choice: the wife of a man, ... the wife of his neighbor: the case is stated twice
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the clause, first in general ("a man's wife") and then more narrowly ("his neighbor's wife"). It may be a deliberate restatement for emphasis, or the clause may have been copied twice by accident in the course of copying. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: As in 19:18, the neighbor is a fellow Israelite.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת־אֵ֣שֶׁת אָבִ֔יו עֶרְוַ֥ת אָבִ֖יו גִּלָּ֑ה מֽוֹת־יוּמְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם דְּמֵיהֶ֥ם בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who lies with [the] wife of his father, [the] nakedness of his father he has uncovered; surely they will be put to death both of them; their blood [is] on them.
pieces: If a man has sexual relations with his father's wife, he has committed an offense against his father. Both of them must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own.

L.11: And a man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness; both of them will surely be put to death; their blood [is] on them.

R.11: If a man has sexual relations with his father's wife, he has done a wrong against his father. Both of them must be put to death. They are to blame for their own deaths.

decisions.choice: lies with his father's wife ... has uncovered his father's nakedness: a sexual wrong against his father
decisions.reason: On "uncover the nakedness" see 18:6. As in 18:8, the nakedness of the father's wife is called the father's own nakedness, because husband and wife are one flesh (Genesis 2:24). The woman may be the man's stepmother; the law of 18:7 deals with his own mother.

decisions.choice: their blood is on them: they bear the guilt for their own deaths
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: has sexual relations with; an offense against his father (Balanced) / a wrong against his father (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lies with" and "uncovered his father's nakedness". When the nakedness is said to belong to another man, Balanced and Readable say that the act wrongs him, as in chapter 18. The same wording is used in verses 20-21.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת־כַּלָּת֔וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמְת֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם תֶּ֥בֶל עָשׂ֖וּ דְּמֵיהֶ֥ם בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who lies with his daughter-in-law, surely they will be put to death both of them; confusion they have done; their blood [is] on them.
pieces: If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have done a perverse mixing; the guilt for their deaths is their own.

L.12: And a man who lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them will surely be put to death; they have done a confusion; their blood [is] on them.

R.12: If a man has sexual relations with his son's wife, both of them must be put to death. They have mixed what must be kept apart. They are to blame for their own deaths.

decisions.choice: confusion: a perversion that mixes what God has kept apart
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root for mixing. It is used only here and in 18:23, of a person lying with an animal. A man who takes his son's wife confuses the bonds of the family (18:15).

decisions.choice: their blood is on them
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: his son's wife; mixed what must be kept apart
decisions.reason: Readable explains "daughter-in-law" and the word for confusion. Balanced says "a perverse mixing", as at 18:23.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכַּ֤ב אֶת־זָכָר֙ מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אִשָּׁ֔ה תּוֹעֵבָ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם מ֥וֹת יוּמָ֖תוּ דְּמֵיהֶ֥ם בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who lies with [a] male [the] lyings of [a] woman, [an] abomination they have done both of them; surely they will be put to death; their blood [is] on them.
pieces: If a man lies with a male as a man lies with a woman, the two of them have done a detestable act. They must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own.

L.13: And a man who lies with a male [as with] the lyings of a woman, both of them have done an abomination; they will surely be put to death; their blood [is] on them.

R.13: If a man has sexual relations with another man as he would with a woman, the two of them have done a disgusting thing. They must be put to death. They are to blame for their own deaths.

decisions.choice: lies with a male as with a woman: has sexual relations with another man
decisions.reason: The wording repeats 18:22, where the act is forbidden. "The lyings of a woman" means the way a man lies with a woman. Here the penalty is given, and both men are held guilty.

decisions.choice: an abomination: something the LORD finds detestable
their blood is on them
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקַּ֧ח אֶת־אִשָּׁ֛ה וְאֶת־אִמָּ֖הּ זִמָּ֣ה הִ֑וא בָּאֵ֞שׁ יִשְׂרְפ֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ וְאֶתְהֶ֔ן וְלֹא־תִהְיֶ֥ה זִמָּ֖ה בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who takes [a] woman and her mother, wickedness [is] it; with fire they will burn him and them, and not will be wickedness among you.
pieces: A man who marries a woman and her mother as well has committed depravity. He and the two women are to be burned with fire. Then such depravity will not remain among you.

L.14: And a man who takes a woman and her mother, it [is] depravity; with fire they will burn him and them, so that there will be no depravity among you.

R.14: A man must not marry both a woman and her mother. That is a shameful, evil thing. If he does, he and both women must be burned in a fire. Then this evil will not be found among you.

decisions.choice: takes a woman and her mother: marries both, or takes both as wives
decisions.reason: To take a woman is to marry her (21:7, 13-14). The law of 18:17 forbids it. Whether the marriages are at the same time or one after the other, the man joins himself to a mother and her daughter.

decisions.choice: depravity: a shameful, deliberately evil act
decisions.reason: The word is used in 18:17 of the same act, and in 19:29 of a land filled with prostitution. It names a planned and shameful wrong.

decisions.choice: with fire they will burn him and them: the penalty of burning
decisions.reason: Burning is named only here and in 21:9 in Leviticus. Some take it to mean burning after death by stoning, as with Achan, who was stoned and then burned (Joshua 7:15, 25); the text does not say. "Him and them" means the man and both women.

decisions.choice: A man must not marry both ... If he does,
decisions.reason: Readable states the forbidden act first and then the penalty.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן שְׁכָבְתּ֛וֹ בִּבְהֵמָ֖ה מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה תַּהֲרֹֽגוּ׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who gives his lying in [an] animal, surely he will be put to death, and the animal you will kill.
pieces: A man who has intercourse with an animal must be put to death, and you are to kill the animal as well.

L.15: And a man who gives his lying with an animal will surely be put to death, and you will kill the animal.

R.15: If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he must be put to death. You must also kill the animal.

decisions.choice: gives his lying with an animal: has sexual relations with an animal
decisions.reason: The same expression is used in 18:23, where the act is forbidden. Here the penalty is set.

decisions.choice: you will kill the animal: the animal is destroyed too
decisions.reason: The animal bears no guilt, but it has been part of the act and is put to death with the man, as an ox that kills a person is put to death (Exodus 21:28).

records.source: וְאִשָּׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּקְרַ֤ב אֶל־כָּל־בְּהֵמָה֙ לְרִבְעָ֣ה אֹתָ֔הּ וְהָרַגְתָּ֥ אֶת־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָ֑ה מ֥וֹת יוּמָ֖תוּ דְּמֵיהֶ֥ם בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] woman who draws near to any animal to lie with it, and you will kill the woman and the animal; surely they will be put to death; their blood [is] on them.
pieces: When a woman goes to an animal to mate with it, you must kill the woman and the animal. Both must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own.

L.16: And a woman who draws near to any animal to mate with it, you will kill the woman and the animal; they will surely be put to death; their blood [is] on them.

R.16: A woman might go to an animal to have sexual relations with it. Then you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death. They are to blame for their own deaths.

decisions.choice: draws near to an animal to mate with it: offers herself to an animal
decisions.reason: The verb for mating is the one used in 18:23 and 19:19 of animals. The law for a woman stands beside the law for a man in verse 15, as in 18:23.

decisions.choice: their blood is on them
decisions.reason: As in verse 9. Here the phrase includes the animal.

records.source: וְאִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִקַּ֣ח אֶת־אֲחֹת֡וֹ בַּת־אָבִ֣יו א֣וֹ בַת־אִ֠מּוֹ וְרָאָ֨ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָ֜הּ וְהִֽיא־תִרְאֶ֤ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתוֹ֙ חֶ֣סֶד ה֔וּא וְנִ֨כְרְת֔וּ לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י עַמָּ֑ם עֶרְוַ֧ת אֲחֹת֛וֹ גִּלָּ֖ה עֲוֺנ֥וֹ יִשָּֽׂא׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who takes his sister, [the] daughter of his father or [the] daughter of his mother, and he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, [a] shame [is] it, and they will be cut off before [the] eyes of [the] sons of their people; [the] nakedness of his sister he has uncovered; his iniquity he will bear.
pieces: If a man marries his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of their people. He has had sexual relations with his sister, and he will bear the consequences of his guilt.

L.17: And a man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it [is] a disgrace, and they will be cut off before the eyes of the sons of their people; he has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he will bear his iniquity.

R.17: A man might marry his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they might have sexual relations. That is a disgrace. They must be removed from the people while everyone watches. He has had sexual relations with his sister. He is guilty and will be punished.

decisions.choice: takes his sister ... sees her nakedness and she sees his: marries her and has sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: "Takes" means to take as a wife (verse 14). To see someone's nakedness means here to have sexual relations, in the sense of "uncover the nakedness" (18:6). The sister may be a full sister or a half sister (18:9, 11).

decisions.choice: a disgrace: a shameful thing
decisions.reason: This word is a rare second word with the same letters as the common word for steadfast love. It means a reproach or disgrace, as in Proverbs 14:34.

decisions.choice: they will be cut off in the sight of their people ... he will bear his iniquity: public punishment, and guilt that he must carry
decisions.reason: "Before the eyes of" their people means publicly; on being cut off see 7:20. To bear one's iniquity is to carry the guilt of a wrong and its punishment (5:1; 17:16). Where no human penalty is set, as here and in verses 19-20, the punishment is left to God. Verses 19 and 20 use the same phrase, and verse 20 adds that the offenders will die childless.

decisions.choice: have sexual relations
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "see her nakedness" and "uncovered his sister's nakedness". Balanced and Readable say what both mean, as at 18:6.

decisions.choice: bear the consequences of his guilt (Balanced); is guilty and will be punished (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 17:16.

records.source: וְ֠אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִשְׁכַּ֨ב אֶת־אִשָּׁ֜ה דָּוָ֗ה וְגִלָּ֤ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ֙ אֶת־מְקֹרָ֣הּ הֶֽעֱרָ֔ה וְהִ֕יא גִּלְּתָ֖ה אֶת־מְק֣וֹר דָּמֶ֑יהָ וְנִכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who lies with [a] woman [who is] menstruating and he uncovers her nakedness, her spring he has made naked, and she has uncovered [the] spring of her blood(s), and they will be cut off both of them from [the] midst of their people.
pieces: If a man lies with a woman during her monthly period and has sexual relations with her, he has bared the place her blood flows from, and she has let it be uncovered. Both of them must be cut off from the people.

L.18: And a man who lies with a woman [in her] sickness and uncovers her nakedness has laid bare her spring, and she has uncovered the spring of her blood; and both of them will be cut off from among their people.

R.18: A man must not have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly bleeding. If he does, he has uncovered the place where her blood flows, and she has let him do it. Both of them must be removed from the people.

decisions.choice: a woman in her sickness: a woman during her monthly period
decisions.reason: The word means faint or unwell, and is used of the weakness of a woman's monthly period (15:33). The act is forbidden in 18:19.

decisions.choice: her spring ... the spring of her blood: the source of her bleeding
decisions.reason: "Spring" is used of a woman's flow of blood, as in 12:7. Both the man and the woman knowingly expose it, so both are held guilty.

decisions.choice: they will be cut off: removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: As in 7:20. In 15:24 a man who lies with a woman during her period becomes unclean for seven days, with no other penalty. That law seems to deal with a case the man did not know of or did not intend; this one deals with a deliberate act.

decisions.choice: A man must not ... If he does,
decisions.reason: Readable states the forbidden act first, as in 18:19, and then the penalty.

records.source: וְעֶרְוַ֨ת אֲח֧וֹת אִמְּךָ֛ וַאֲח֥וֹת אָבִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה כִּ֧י אֶת־שְׁאֵר֛וֹ הֶעֱרָ֖ה עֲוֺנָ֥ם יִשָּֽׂאוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] nakedness of [the] sister of your mother and [the] sister of your father not you will uncover, for his relative he has made naked; their iniquity they will bear.
pieces: Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister, for that is to lay bare a close relative. They will bear the consequences of their guilt.

L.19: And you will not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, for he has laid bare his own flesh; they will bear their iniquity.

R.19: Do not have sexual relations with your aunt, your mother's sister or your father's sister. That would be sex with a close relative. Both people would be guilty and would be punished.

decisions.choice: you will not uncover: the law turns to a direct command
decisions.reason: This verse repeats the commands of 18:12-13 in their own form ("you") and does not set a penalty for the community to carry out. The guilt is left with the offenders.

decisions.choice: his relative: his own flesh, a close blood relative
decisions.reason: The word means flesh, and so a near relative (18:6, 12-13). The aunt is related by blood, unlike the aunt by marriage in verse 20.

decisions.choice: they will bear their iniquity
decisions.reason: See verse 17.

decisions.choice: your aunt
decisions.reason: Readable names the relation and then explains it.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת־דֹּ֣דָת֔וֹ עֶרְוַ֥ת דֹּד֖וֹ גִּלָּ֑ה חֶטְאָ֥ם יִשָּׂ֖אוּ עֲרִירִ֥ים יָמֻֽתוּ׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who lies with his aunt, [the] nakedness of his uncle he has uncovered; their sin they will bear; childless they will die.
pieces: If a man has sexual relations with his uncle's wife, he has committed an offense against his uncle. They will bear the consequences of their sin and die without children.

L.20: And a man who lies with his aunt has uncovered his uncle's nakedness; they will bear their sin; they will die childless.

R.20: If a man has sexual relations with his uncle's wife, he has done a wrong against his uncle. They will be punished for their sin. They will die without having children.

decisions.choice: his aunt: his father's brother's wife
decisions.reason: The word means the wife of one's uncle, as the next clause shows ("his uncle's nakedness"). See 18:14.

decisions.choice: they will bear their sin; they will die childless: God himself will punish them by denying them children
decisions.reason: No human penalty is set. Instead the punishment is left to God, and it fits the sin: those who have joined themselves wrongly within the family will have no family to come after them. To die childless was a great loss, since a man's name lived on through his children (Genesis 15:2; Deuteronomy 25:6; Jeremiah 22:30). The word is rare; it may mean that they will have no children, or that the children born of the union will not count as theirs and will not carry on their name.

decisions.choice: his uncle's wife
decisions.reason: Literal says "his aunt". Balanced and Readable say "his uncle's wife", so that the reader does not take her to be a blood relative, as in verse 19.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִקַּ֛ח אֶת־אֵ֥שֶׁת אָחִ֖יו נִדָּ֣ה הִ֑וא עֶרְוַ֥ת אָחִ֛יו גִּלָּ֖ה עֲרִירִ֥ים יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And [a] man who takes [the] wife of his brother, impurity [is] it; [the] nakedness of his brother he has uncovered; childless they will be.
pieces: A man who marries his brother's wife does an unclean thing. He has committed an offense against his brother; the two of them will be childless.

L.21: And a man who takes his brother's wife, it [is] impurity; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they will be childless.

R.21: A man must not marry his brother's wife. That is an unclean thing to do. He has done a wrong against his brother. The man and the woman will not have children.

decisions.choice: impurity: something unclean and repulsive
decisions.reason: The word is used for a woman's monthly uncleanness (15:19-20) and, as here, for what is morally unclean (Ezra 9:11). The act is forbidden in 18:16.

decisions.choice: takes his brother's wife: marries her, whether the brother is alive and divorced or has died
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 25:5-10 gives one exception: when a brother dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up a son to carry on the dead man's name (compare Genesis 38:8; Ruth 4:5). The general law here forbids such a marriage in every other case.

decisions.choice: they will be childless
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־כָּל־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְלֹא־תָקִ֤יא אֶתְכֶם֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֛ם שָׁ֖מָּה לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And you will keep all my statutes and all my judgments and you will do them, and not will vomit you the land where I [am] bringing you there to dwell in it.
pieces: Keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, and carry them out. Then the land to which I am bringing you to make your home will not vomit you out.

L.22: And you will keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to dwell in it will not vomit you out.

R.22: Obey all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. Do what they say. Then the land where I am taking you to live will not throw you out the way a person vomits.

decisions.choice: my statutes and my judgments: all God's laws
decisions.reason: On these words see 18:4. Together they cover the whole of what God commands.

decisions.choice: the land will vomit you out: the land itself will drive out a people who defile it
decisions.reason: The land is pictured as a living body that cannot keep down the people who make it unclean. 18:25-28 says it has done so to the peoples before Israel and will do so to Israel too.

decisions.choice: throw you out the way a person vomits
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א תֵֽלְכוּ֙ בְּחֻקֹּ֣ת הַגּ֔וֹי אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֤י אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ עָשׂ֔וּ וָאָקֻ֖ץ בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And not you will walk in [the] statutes of the nation which I [am] sending away from before you, for all these [things] they have done, and I loathed them.
pieces: Do not follow the practices of the nation I am driving out ahead of you. They did all these things, and I came to loathe them.

L.23: And you will not walk in the statutes of the nation which I am sending away from before you, for they have done all these [things], and I loathed them.

R.23: Do not live the way the nations live. I am forcing them out of the land as you arrive. They did all these things, so I came to hate them.

decisions.choice: walk in the statutes of the nation: live by the customs of the peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: To walk is to live in a certain way. The "statutes" here are the customs of the people living in the land, the practices of chapters 18 and 20 (18:3, 24-30). "Nation" is a collective singular for all the peoples there. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint have the plural, "the nations".

decisions.choice: I am sending them away ... I loathed them: God drives out the peoples of the land because of their sins
decisions.reason: The peoples of Canaan lose the land because of what they did, not because Israel is more deserving (18:24-25; Deuteronomy 9:4-5; Genesis 15:16). The word "loathe" is used again in 26:43-44, where God says he will not finally reject Israel.

decisions.choice: practices (Balanced); the way the nations live (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "statutes", the word used for God's laws in verse 22, to show the contrast. Balanced says "practices", since these are customs, not God's laws.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֣ר לָכֶ֗ם אַתֶּם֮ תִּֽירְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אַדְמָתָם֒ וַאֲנִ֞י אֶתְּנֶ֤נָּה לָכֶם֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֹתָ֔הּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הִבְדַּ֥לְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִן־הָֽעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And I have said to you, you, you will take possession of their ground, and I, I will give it to you to take possession of it, [a] land flowing [with] milk and honey. I [am] Yahweh your God who has separated you from the peoples.
pieces: I have told you that you will take over their land; I myself will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; I have set you apart from the other peoples.

L.24: And I have said to you, You will take possession of their land, and I, I will give it to you to possess it, a land flowing [with] milk and honey. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

R.24: I have promised you that you will take their land. I will give it to you to own. It is a rich land, flowing with milk and honey. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I have set you apart from the other nations.

decisions.choice: a land flowing with milk and honey: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: The phrase first comes in God's promise to Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:8, 17). Milk stands for good pasture for flocks and herds, and honey for sweetness and plenty; the honey may be from bees or from fruit such as dates.

decisions.choice: who has separated you from the peoples: God has set Israel apart from all other peoples to be his own
decisions.reason: The verb means to divide or make a distinction. God "separated" light from darkness at creation (Genesis 1:4), and the priests are to separate holy from common and clean from unclean (10:10; 11:47). In the same way God has separated Israel from the other peoples, so that they will be his own people (verse 26; Exodus 19:5-6; 1 Kings 8:53). Verse 25 draws the conclusion: because God has separated them, they must separate clean animals from unclean. The food laws of chapter 11 are a daily sign that Israel belongs to God and not to the peoples around them.

decisions.choice: you ... I: both pronouns are emphatic
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses both "you" (you will possess) and "I" (I will give). Israel will take the land, but only as God's gift.

decisions.choice: set you apart
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "separated" to show the link with verse 25 and with 10:10. Balanced and Readable say "set apart", the sense when God separates a people for himself.

decisions.choice: It is a rich land
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of milk and honey means before giving it.

records.source: וְהִבְדַּלְתֶּ֞ם בֵּֽין־הַבְּהֵמָ֤ה הַטְּהֹרָה֙ לַטְּמֵאָ֔ה וּבֵין־הָע֥וֹף הַטָּמֵ֖א לַטָּהֹ֑ר וְלֹֽא־תְשַׁקְּצ֨וּ אֶת־נַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶ֜ם בַּבְּהֵמָ֣ה וּבָע֗וֹף וּבְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְמֹ֣שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הִבְדַּ֥לְתִּי לָכֶ֖ם לְטַמֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: And you will separate between the animal[s] clean and unclean, and between the bird[s] unclean and clean, and not you will make detestable yourselves by animal[s] and by bird[s] and by all that creeps [on] the ground, which I have separated for you to [declare] unclean.
pieces: So you must distinguish between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not make yourselves detestable through any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, the creatures I have marked off for you as unclean.

L.25: And you will separate between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean, and you will not make yourselves detestable by animal or by bird or by anything that creeps [on] the ground, which I have separated for you as unclean.

R.25: So you must keep clean animals and birds apart from unclean ones. Do not make yourselves disgusting by eating any animal or bird or creature that crawls on the ground that I have told you is unclean.

decisions.choice: you will separate ... which I have separated for you: Israel's separation mirrors God's
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 24 is used twice more. God has separated Israel from the peoples, and so Israel is to separate clean from unclean animals, as God has separated them (chapter 11). The order of the pairs is reversed (clean and unclean, unclean and clean), a pattern that marks the two as complete opposites.

decisions.choice: make yourselves detestable: make yourselves loathsome by eating what is unclean
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in 11:43, from the word "detestable" (11:10). Eating unclean creatures makes the eater unclean and unfit for God's presence (11:44).

decisions.choice: clean and unclean
by eating
decisions.reason: Readable says how a person becomes unclean through these creatures, as chapter 11 explains.

records.source: וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לִי֙ קְדֹשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י קָד֖וֹשׁ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וָאַבְדִּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִן־הָֽעַמִּ֖ים לִהְי֥וֹת לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And you will be to me holy, for holy [am] I, Yahweh, and I have separated you from the peoples to belong to me.
pieces: You must be holy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am holy. I have set you apart from the other peoples so that you will belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.26: And you will be holy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for holy [am] I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I have separated you from the peoples to be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

R.26: You must be holy and belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am holy. I have set you apart from the other nations to be my very own people.

decisions.choice: you will be holy to me, for I am holy: Israel's holiness reflects God's
decisions.reason: On the call to be holy because the LORD is holy see 11:44 and 19:2. "To me" adds that Israel's holiness means belonging to the LORD. The chapter's laws on Molech, mediums and sexual conduct are part of this holiness.

decisions.choice: I have separated you from the peoples to be mine: God set Israel apart so that they would belong to him
decisions.reason: As in verse 24. The purpose is now stated: to belong to God, his own treasured people (Exodus 19:5-6; Deuteronomy 7:6; 14:2).

decisions.choice: set you apart
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

records.source: וְאִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֨ה בָהֶ֥ם א֛וֹב א֥וֹ יִדְּעֹנִ֖י מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑תוּ בָּאֶ֛בֶן יִרְגְּמ֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם דְּמֵיהֶ֥ם בָּֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And [a] man or [a] woman, if there is in them [a] medium or [a] spiritist, surely they will be put to death; with stone[s] they will stone them; their blood [is] on them.
pieces: A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist must be put to death. They are to be stoned; the guilt for their deaths is their own.'"

L.27: And a man or a woman, if there is in them a medium or a spiritist, they will surely be put to death; they will stone them with stones; their blood [is] on them.'"

R.27: Any man or woman who says they can talk with the dead or with spirits must be put to death. People must throw stones at them until they die. They are to blame for their own deaths.'"

decisions.choice: if there is in them a medium or a spiritist: if they practice as a medium or consult spirits
decisions.reason: The words are those of verse 6 and 19:31. "In them" may mean that the person is thought to have such a spirit within, speaking through them, or simply that the person acts as a medium. Verse 6 punished those who consult mediums; this verse punishes the mediums themselves.

decisions.choice: surely put to death ... stone them: the community carries out the sentence
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. Saul had put the mediums out of the land, but then went to one himself (1 Samuel 28:3, 7-9).

decisions.choice: their blood is on them
decisions.reason: As in verse 9. The speech that began in verse 2 ends here.

decisions.choice: throw stones at them until they die
decisions.reason: As at verse 2.
